item.title: Reconciling anomalous quadrupole deformation in $^{200,202}$Hg with Coulomb excitation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stable isotopes of mercury, with two fewer protons than magic lead, are found experimentally to exhibit oblate deformation, similar to neighbouring platinum isotopes. These isotopes are of special interest due to the use of $^{199}$Hg as an experimental laboratory for electric dipole moment searches, which are a powerful test of charge-parity ($CP$) violation and the interpretation of which depends critically on the quadrupole and octopule shapes of the underlying nucleus. It is observed that the ratio between experimental quadrupole moments and electric quadrupole transition strengths exceed physical limits, placing uncertainty on this underlying shape. In an effort to resolve this situation, a Coulomb excitation experiment was performed to remeasure the spectroscopic quadrupole moment ($Q_s(2^+_1)$) of $^{200}$Hg and $^{202}$Hg utilising $^{48}$Ti and $^{120}$Sn targets. The values obtained were $Q_s(2^+_1)$ $^{200,202}$Hg = $0.52(14)$, $0.63(10)$ eb, lying within physical limits defined by $B(E2)$ values but still consistent with near axially-symmetric oblate deformation. A systematic study of nuclei indicates that, as with neighbouring Pt isotopes, $^{200,202}$Hg are strongly oblate deformed, albeit without fully developing into an axial rotor.

item.title: The $b\bar{b}c\bar{c}$ Fully Heavy Tetraquark at the LHC and the FCC: Multimodal Fragmentation and Observability
item.description: arXiv:2610.27396v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the production of the all-heavy mixed-flavor $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark through a multimodal fragmentation setup combining direct-multiquark and scalar-diquark mechanisms. Standard Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) evolution is applied while preserving threshold consistency through the Heavy-Flavor NonRelativistic evolution (HF-NRevo) scheme. The resulting fragmentation functions (FFs) are then embedded into hybrid high-energy and collinear factorization at next-to-leading order for semi-inclusive tetraquark-plus-jet production. We compare the two mechanisms through rapidity-separation distributions at the 14 TeV High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) and at the 100 TeV Future Circular Collider (FCC), finding a clear phenomenological preference for the direct-multiquark channel over the scalar-diquark mode. Integrated cross sections and expected event yields provide favorable production-level prospects for future searches at the HL-LHC, with substantially enhanced statistics at FCC energies. These results establish a quantitative connection between microscopic formation mechanisms and the prospective observability of the $b\bar b c\bar c$ tetraquark at present and future hadron colliders.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao V. Bulh\~oes, Francesco G. Celiberto, Victor P. Gon\c{c}alves

item.title: A Radiation-Hardened, Fault-Aware Quantized Neural Network That Self-Heals
item.description: arXiv:2610.27621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning (DL) models are increasingly being deployed into radiation-challenging environments in spacecraft, particle accelerators, and, soon, space-based data centers. Instantiated as a learned orchestration of numbers stored in persistent memory, models are susceptible to continual degradation as high-energy particles corrupt data. At inference time, new data passed through the network fundamentally break the off-line assumptions and guarantees of a static model determined during training. To preserve the quality and efficacy of the models, fault tolerance against bit flips is a clear objective. In this work we developed a runtime method for repairing the quantized weights of neural networks (NNs) after bit flips on commodity, commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware, without storing extra replicas. Our work extends the well-established Fault-Aware Training (FAT) paradigm by adding an alignment penalty to concentrate undamaged activations and weights into a low-rank subspace, and we then reconstruct flagged corrupted coordinates from the uncorrupted survivors. We call this method {\it Projection Healing} and apply it to six regression benchmarks on quantized NNs. Holding a FAT checkpoint fixed and toggling only the runtime heal gives a further ${\sim}23\%$ reduction in the native-unit excess integral. Across those datasets the method extends the operational scrub interval by a median of $2.04\times$ at a $+5\%$ RMSE degradation and $1.96\times$ at $+50\%$, compared with $1.62\times$ and $1.07\times$ for classical Single Error Correction, Double Error Detection (SECDED). This introduces a new path towards designing resilient data-driven models, complementing established hardware redundancy, ECC, and FAT-based techniques.
item.dc:creator: Peter Xiangyuan Ma, Joshua S. Bloom

item.title: From Harmonic Oscillators to Multiplicity Distributions in Particle Production Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.27955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose an oscillator framework of studying multi-particle production processes using the information theory approach. For a system of degenerate oscillators, we derive the negative binomial distribution (NBD) and its nonadditive generalization represented as gNBD. We observe that gNBD derived from nonadditive statistics describes data in higher multiplicity region, thereby providing an alternative for the multi-component distributions used in phenomenological studies. We also generalize our framework for non-degenerate oscillators and encounter a Lerch-type generalization of the Barnes zeta function that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been studied in the context of nonadditive statistics and multiplicity studies before.
item.dc:creator: Trambak Bhattacharyya, Maciej Rybczy\'{n}ski, Zbigniew W{\l}odarczyk

item.title: Shell-model description of collective deformation variables $\beta$ and $\gamma$ in $^{164-188}$Hf nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2610.28509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetry-based models, such as the pseudo-SU(3) scheme, have proved to be highly useful tools for describing the low-energy structure of nuclei in the rare-earth region. This model is employed to study the evolution of the collective deformation variables beta and gamma in the ground state (0+) along the isotopic chain 164-188Hf. The truncation is carried out by considering the irreducible representations (irreps) with high spatial symmetry and pseudo-spin 0 and 1, so that both the most and less symmetric relevant irreps are included, the latter being of particular importance for the description of low-energy properties, especially the shape transition. The Hamiltonian includes spherical Nilsson single-particle energies, the quadrupole-quadrupole interaction, and pairing correlations. It is parameterised in a systematic manner, so that the description is obtained without free parameters. In agreement with experimental data, the maximum deformation beta occurs at N = 100, although the model predicts values that are about 20% smaller. As in other theoretical studies, a prolate deformation (gamma = 8o) is predicted for almost all nuclei in the shell, with a clear transition towards triaxial shapes for N > 110. An analysis of the effects of the pairing and Nilsson terms on the values of $\beta$ and gamma indicates that it is the latter that determine the prolate-oblate transition, with the pairing term playing only a marginal role. The absence of nucleons in the intruder sector is the most significant limitation of the model.
item.dc:creator: Carlos E. Vargas

item.title: High-Precision Mass Measurements of 52Ni and 51Co Reveal Breakdown of the Isobaric Multiplet Mass Equation in the f p Shell
item.description: arXiv:2607.09986v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We performed high-precision mass measurements of the proton-rich nuclei $^{52}$Ni and $^{51}$Co with the LEBIT Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). For $^{52}$Ni, a mass excess of $-22474.8(2.2)$~keV was determined, which is consistent with a recent storage-ring measurement at the Cooler-Storage Ring (CSRe) but has a factor 37 improved precision. For $^{51}$Co, we obtained a mass excess of $-27375.1(5.7)$~keV, agreeing with a recent CSRe result, while reducing the uncertainty by a factor~2. Combining our mass value for $^{52}$Ni with the known two-proton decay energy of $^{54}$Zn, we determined the mass excess of $^{54}$Zn to be $-6463(42)$~keV. These new mass values reveal a substantial breakdown of the isobaric mass multiplet equation for $A=52$ and $A=54$, and provide stringent benchmarks for isospin-symmetry-breaking effects in the proton-rich $fp$-shell, favoring theoretical descriptions that omit the Coulomb-exchange term.
item.dc:creator: F. M. Maier, G. Bollen, B. A. Brown, S. E. Campbell, X. Chen, H. Erington, N. D. Gamage, K. Godbey, C. M. Ireland, C. Izzo, R. Ringle, C. S. Sumithrarachchi, A. C. C. Villari

item.title: Measurements of local polarization of $\Lambda$ hyperons with event shape engineering in Au+Au collisions at RHIC-STAR
item.description: arXiv:2610.25989v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Anisotropic flow is expected to generate local vorticities along the beam direction, which in turn lead to local polarization of produced particles. Although the local polarization of hyperons has already been observed at RHIC and the LHC, its mechanism is not yet understood: model calculations indicate that the shear-induced and vorticity-induced contributions can have opposite signs and may substantially cancel, so that the resulting polarization depends sensitively on the theoretical implementation. Since both are driven by the anisotropic flow, we employ the Event Shape Engineering (ESE) method, which selects events with different flow magnitudes within a narrow centrality range, to measure the local polarization as a function of the elliptic flow at a fixed multiplicity. We report the measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_2$) and the local polarization ($P_{z,2}$) of $\Lambda$ and $\bar{\Lambda}$ as a function of the reduced flow vector magnitude $q_2$ used for the ESE event selection, in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 19.6~{\rm GeV}$ from the STAR experiment. The $v_2$ shows a clear positive dependence on $q_2$, while $P_{z,2}$ indicates a weak positive dependence on $q_2$ and $v_2$. This is the first measurement to directly investigate the relation between anisotropic flow and local polarization, providing new insight into the origin of local polarization.
item.dc:creator: Taiki Kondo (for the STAR Collaboration)

item.title: New Bounds on Heavy QCD Axions from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
item.description: arXiv:2510.23695v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) constraints on heavy QCD axions. BBN offers a powerful probe of new physics that modifies the neutron-to-proton ratio during the process, thanks to the precisely measured primordial Helium-4 abundance. A heavy QCD axion provides an attractive target for this probe, because not only is it a well-motivated hypothetical particle by the strong CP problem, but also it dominantly decays to hadrons if kinematically allowed. A range of its lifetime is thus excluded where the hadronic decays would significantly alter the neutron-to-proton ratio. We compute axion-induced modification of the neutron-to-proton ratio, and obtain robust upper bounds on the axion lifetimes, as low as 0.017 s for the axion mass higher than 300 MeV. Remarkably, this is stronger than projected future CMB bounds via $N_{\rm eff}$. Our bounds are largely insensitive to uncertainties in hadronic cross sections and the axion's branching fractions into various hadrons, as well as to the precise value of the initial axion abundance. We also incorporate, for the first time, several key improvements, such as scattering processes by energetic $K_L$ and secondary hadrons, that can also be important for studying general hadronic injections during BBN, not limited to those from axion decays.
item.dc:creator: Tae Hyun Jung, Takemichi Okui, Kohsaku Tobioka, Jiabao Wang

item.title: Nonflow Subtraction Beyond Two-Particle Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2606.10258v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Establishing collective flow in small collision systems is a crucial and necessary condition for pinning down the minimum conditions for quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formation. In two-particle correlations, nonflow has been subtracted with good control, pushing the reach of flow measurements down to very small event particle multiplicity $N$. However, the multi-particle nature of collectivity has not been established in the same $N$ regime, because the residual nonflow surviving the subevent procedure in multi-particle cumulants has never been quantified. We develop a general nonflow subtraction framework for $m$-particle cumulants, built around the approximate $1/N^{m-1}$ scaling of nonflow in the independent-source picture. Correlators containing $v_1$ serve as nonflow-dominated estimators, since the $p_{\mathrm T}$-integrated dipolar flow is expected to be small. Using HIJING as a controlled nonflow-only environment, we test the subtraction for three target observables ($\langle v_2^2\rangle$, $\langle v_2^2\delta p_{\mathrm T}\rangle$, and $c_2\{4\}$) in O+O at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$ TeV and 200 GeV and in $d$+Au at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 200$ GeV. Most of the nonflow is removed, with residual fractions typically within 20-30% when converted to the two-particle level, though the best estimator differs across the three targets. We identify a multiplicity-reweighting correction, previously overlooked in two-particle correlations, that explains the long-standing undersubtraction of the naive $1/N$-scaling method; its impact grows as a power of the correlator order. The framework gives a systematic route to nonflow subtraction beyond two-particle correlations, broadening the class of multi-particle observables accessible to the small-system flow program.
item.dc:creator: Zaining Wang, Jiangyong Jia, Jinhui Chen, Shengli Huang, Chunjian Zhang, Zhengxi Yan

item.title: A New Scaling of Neutron Star Tidal Deformability for Directly Probing the Central Equation of State Parameter
item.description: arXiv:2606.21402v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The dimensionless tidal deformability, $\Lambda$, of neutron stars (NSs), inferred from gravitational-wave (GW) observations, has thus far been used primarily to constrain the pressure of dense matter near twice nuclear saturation density, leaving the core equation of state (EOS) largely inaccessible to inspiral-phase GW observations. We show that a fundamental central EOS parameter can be probed directly through $\Lambda$ using a perturbative analysis of the dimensionless stellar-structure and tidal-response equations formulated in terms of scaled intrinsic variables, without invoking any specific EOS model. We uncover a remarkable EOS-insensitive scaling relation between $\Lambda$ and the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}\equiv P_{\rm c}/\varepsilon_{\rm c}$, where $P_{\rm c}$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm c}$ denote the central pressure and energy density, respectively. The relation is validated against a broad ensemble of physically viable EOSs. Applying it to tidal deformabilities inferred from events such as GW170817 enables a direct determination of $\rm{X}$. By adopting the previously established effective upper bound $\rm{X}\lesssim0.381$, we infer a tight lower bound, $\Lambda_{\rm{TOV}}\gtrsim9.1^{+0.5}_{-0.5}$, for maximum-mass NSs along stable mass-radius sequences, quantitatively demonstrating that even the most compact stable NSs remain distinctly separated from black holes, for which $\Lambda_{\rm{BH}}=0$. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized connection between inspiral-phase tidal deformability and the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}$, establishing a direct link between GW observables and the microphysics of ultradense matter in the strong-gravity regime. The resulting scaling establishes inspiral-phase tidal deformability as a direct and largely model-insensitive probe of the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}$, and hence of key properties of NS cores.
item.dc:creator: Jian-Hao Shi, Bao-Jun Cai, Bao-An Li, Yu-Gang Ma
